name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd
title: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd - 524715 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Sun Pharma Q4 FY26 is a branded-innovation story with generics still lagging: US sales fell 1.1%, FY27 guided to high single-digit growth, and no explicit margin guidance after Organon deal.

triggers.label: Greenfield sterile plant for future supply
triggers.quote: the Greenfield facility is to address what we foresee as the future requirement to continue to be able to support the business across the world

triggers.label: Innovative Medicines US crossed $1 billion
triggers.quote: Innovative Medicines crossed $1 billion for the first time in the United States

triggers.label: EBITDA margin down QoQ to 27.1%
triggers.quote: EBITDA margins were lower quarter-on-quarter due to several factors

guidance.quote: we expect high single -digit consolidated top line growth for FY27
We expect our FY27 R&D spend to be 6% to 7% of the sales for the next year.
We expect the effective tax rate to be in the range of 25%.
We expect the acquisition to be completed in Q4 FY27.

red_flags.quote: growth in Innovative Medicines was offset by lower sales in the generic business due to additional competition in certain products

summary.headline: Sun Pharma Q4 FY26 sales rose 13.6% to INR 145,598 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 27.1% from 31.9% QoQ; FY27 guided to high single-digit top-line growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated sales were INR 145,598 mn, up 13.6% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 39,542 mn (up 6.4% YoY) and a 27.1% margin, down from 31.9% in Q3. Management attributed the sequential margin drop to lower milestone income, seasonality, lower lenalidomide contribution and elevated spend in several geographies, including the US, which it expects to normalise. FY26 sales reached INR 582 bn (+11.9%) with EBITDA of INR 177,314 mn (+16.1%, 30.3% margin). Management guided to high single-digit consolidated top-line growth for FY27 and R&D at 6-7% of sales, while the Organon acquisition is expected to close in Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +6.4% YoY; margin vs 28.7% YoY and 31.9% QoQ
vs 19.8% Q4 FY25 and 24.3% Q3 FY26

segments.name: Global Innovative Medicines
segments.commentary: Q4 sales USD 354 mn (+20.1%), 22.2% of consolidated sales; FY26 USD 1,420 mn (+16.8%). Global Ilumya FY26 USD 796 mn (+16.7%), excluding alliance partner in-market sales.

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 sales INR 48,359 mn (+14.8%), 33.2% of consolidated sales; FY26 INR 192,904 mn (+14%). Volume growth 6% vs IPM volume growth 1.6%; market share 8.4% (PharmaTrac MAT March 26) vs 8.1% a year earlier.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Q4 sales USD 459 mn (-1.1%), 28.8% of consolidated sales; FY26 USD 1.9 bn with marginal decline. Innovative Medicines crossed USD 1 bn in FY26 and is now larger than US generics, which declined on added competition.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Q4 formulation revenue USD 306 mn (+17.4%; constant currency +6.5%), 19.2% of consolidated revenue. FY26 USD 1,265 mn (+13.6%; constant currency +8.2%).

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Q4 formulation revenue USD 220 mn (+10%), about 13.8% of consolidated revenue. FY26 USD 969 mn (+14.4%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 high single-digit consolidated top-line growth, based on current regulatory and macro view.
FY27 R&D spend 6-7% of sales; Q4 FY26 R&D was INR 9,757 mn (6.7% of sales), with innovative R&D at 36.9% of total.
No explicit EBITDA margin guidance this year; UNLOXCYT and LEQSELVI launch costs are built into the plan as ongoing base spend.
Effective tax rate expected around 25% in FY27 and beyond.
Organon acquisition: integration office set up, regulatory filings in progress, completion expected in Q4 FY27.
No UNLOXCYT or LEQSELVI sales assumed outside the US in FY27.
Tariff impact on branded drugs from Section 232 described as marginal for FY27.
capex_capacity: Greenfield facility under way in Madhya Pradesh, a sterile-only plant for supplying major global markets; not a standalone trigger for US generics volume.
Ilumya BLA for adults with active psoriatic arthritis accepted by US FDA; regulatory action date late October 2026.
Site compliance: US FDA re-inspection timing at Baska or Halol not predictable; sites kept in 24/7 audit readiness.
Semaglutide oral clinical study completed; launch after approval.
demand_pricing: India growth led by volumes and new launches rather than price, in contrast to the market where price is the key driver.

Semaglutide (Noveltreat and Sematrinity) launched in India around 21 March 2026 across strengths with auto-injector and pen; management says prescription share reflection will take 5-6 months and Sun is not yet number one in GLP-1 generics.
US Ilumya growth continued; management says Part B reimbursement is unaffected by biosimilar Stelara formulary changes.
LEQSELVI: majority US market access as of 1 April; testing regimens expanded. A new competitor launch was seen as market-expanding.
UNLOXCYT launched in US in Q4; physician response positive, with repeat purchases from cancer centres and no limited-distribution model.
Generics: management attributes weak growth to compliance-related approval delays and ongoing price erosion.

qa_highlights.question: UNLOXCYT early physician feedback and competitor Part B exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Richard Ascroft said physicians see the expected efficacy with no immune-mediated adverse events, linked to PD-L2 preservation; declined to comment on competitors' Part B strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Semaglutide India traction and oral semaglutide plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Kirti Ganorkar said the launch on 21 March means market data lag; reflection expected in 5-6 months. Oral semaglutide clinical study is complete, with launch after approval.

qa_highlights.question: Sequential margin drop and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayashree Satagopan said Revlimid impact was small; multiple small items drove other expenses, with normalisation expected. Higher spend was across several geographies including the US.

qa_highlights.question: Generics weakness and the Greenfield plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Shanghvi attributed generics weakness to compliance-related approval delays and price erosion; Aalok Shanghvi said the new sterile-only facility is for future capacity, not US generics alone.

qa_highlights.question: R&D split between innovation and generics?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Shanghvi declined to give a split, citing rising innovative R&D; limited residual IP makes large sums hard to commit, so lifecycle management is being accelerated.

qa_highlights.question: Tariffs and FY27 EBITDA trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Richard Ascroft said the impact is marginal for FY27 with mitigation planned. Management gave no margin guidance; launch costs are part of the base spend.

risks_watch: Sequential EBITDA margin compression (31.9% to 27.1%) and whether elevated US and other-geography spend normalises in Q1 FY27.
Generics US and emerging-market growth constrained by compliance-related approval delays and price erosion; re-inspection timing at Baska or Halol unknown.
Competitive pressure on US generics and a possible new LEQSELVI competitor.
Organon acquisition (completion expected Q4 FY27) and integration; Organon results not discussed on this call.
Tariffs on branded drugs under Section 232, with two effective dates in July and September.
summary.management_tone: Confident on innovative medicines, India share gains and the FY27 growth outlook, but guarded on margins and generics, with no explicit EBITDA guidance and deflection on Organon and competitor questions.
key_quotes: Ex-forex, EBITDA margins were lower quarter-on-quarter due to several factors, including lower milestone income, some seasonality, reduced contribution from lenalidomide in Q4 versus Q3 and higher spend in certain geographies, including US.
On the guidance, we expect high single -digit consolidated top line growth for FY27 based on our current understanding of the regulatory and macro environment.
I am pleased to note that this year, we have seen the highest gain in market share for Sun since Ranbaxy acquisition.
So, my expectation is that this will continue to be this.
We are not taking a view that it's -- the other geographies are not attractive.

adds.what: Greenfield sterile-only plant in Madhya Pradesh supplying global markets

growth.why: FY27 guided to high single-digit consolidated top-line growth (~8% midpoint), backed mainly by India volume growth and new launches (UNLOXCYT, LEQSELVI, semaglutide) and Ilumya, with only a sterile Greenfield plant under construction and no specific capacity timing given, so backing is partial.
